role: Swapnil - CEO (product & business) - RC 115f698 product/business investigation
summary: Audit of RC 115f698, read from the clean worktree rc-115f698. Code and the unit tests in the RC's own surefire reports (3621 run, 0 failures, 22 skipped, the skips being the Docker/MySQL integration classes) show that a brand CAN go from signup to a paid campaign with no ops help at almost every step. There are 3 exceptions. (1) Before a campaign can go ACTIVE, an admin has to approve the brand's KYC by hand. The admin cannot see the uploaded GST/PAN documents in the app, and nothing notifies the admin that a KYC is waiting. (2) Approving a deliverable never pays the creator, because Deliverable.milestoneId is never populated. The brand has to press a separate 'release' step. No auto-release job exists, and a brand OWNER/ADMIN can instead refund the funded hold back to its own wallet at any time, including after the work is approved, unless a dispute is already open. (3) The production build ships with creator bank payout (withdraw) switched off (VITE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED=false). So in production 'money in the creator's bank' today means a SUPER_ADMIN pays manually outside the app and records the bank UTR (the transfer reference). Monetization in code is a 10% brand fee on budgetMax charged at publish (7% on Pro), a 15% creator commission deducted at release, and a Pro plan at Rs 4,999/month. Brand wallet money can never leave the platform (no brand withdrawal or refund to source). Creator identity KYC is self-declared and never verified. None of this has been proven at runtime for the RC.

questions.question: Can a brand go from signup to an ACTIVE (live) campaign without anyone on our team doing something?
questions.why_it_matters: Time-to-first-campaign is the activation metric. If a manual gate sits in it, go-live needs a staffed ops queue.
questions.answer: No. Signup is self-serve with an email OTP (one-time code). But publishing a campaign as ACTIVE throws 403 WORKSPACE_NOT_VERIFIED unless the workspace's verificationStatus is VERIFIED, and the only code that sets VERIFIED is the admin action AdminBrandService.verifyKyc. The brand's own KYC submission only sets PENDING and notifies nobody.
questions.evidence: CampaignValidator.validateStatusForWorkspace (CampaignValidator.java:62-68) is called from CampaignService.java:171 and :266. Workspace.applyKyc (Workspace.java:395-401) sets PENDING. OnboardingService.submitBrandKyc (OnboardingService.java:171-183) has no event or notification. AdminBrandService.verifyKyc (AdminBrandService.java:280-319) is the only transition to VERIFIED: workspace.applyKycDecision, requiring SUPER_ADMIN/ADMIN plus MFA. AuthService.brandRegister (AuthService.java:126-249) is self-serve.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: I did not check whether ops has an out-of-band alert, such as a daily admin email digest, that surfaces PENDING brands. Draft campaigns can still be created while unverified.

questions.question: When a brand approves a creator's deliverable, does the creator get paid automatically?
questions.why_it_matters: This is the core promise of 'secured payment'. If approval does not move money, creators wait on a second brand action.
questions.answer: No. ContractService materializes Deliverable rows without milestoneId, so EscrowService.tryReleaseOnApproval always returns held('NO_MILESTONE'). The approval succeeds but no money moves. The brand has to call POST /wallet/escrow/release separately (the 'release' button in deal-payments-tab / brand wallet). No scheduled auto-release exists.
questions.evidence: ContractService.java:765-775 (Deliverable.builder() with no .milestoneId). EscrowService.tryReleaseOnApproval, EscrowService.java:729-732. BrandDeliverableService.java:191 and :221-233 (heldReason/describeUnlinkedHold). BrandDeliverableServiceTest.java:321-323 asserts NO_MILESTONE and passes in the RC surefire report (32 run, 0 failures). A grep for autoRelease/auto-approve across src/main found only CreatorProfile.java.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Not reproduced at runtime. The FE copy may explain the second step clearly, but the money still depends on the brand acting.

questions.question: Can a brand take back funded money after the creator has delivered?
questions.why_it_matters: Creator trust. If 'secured' funds can be clawed back by one side alone, the escrow promise is hollow and creators will churn.
questions.answer: Yes. EscrowService.refund needs only OWNER/ADMIN, a hold in the brand's workspace, status FUNDED, and no active dispute. It never checks deliverable status or whether the brand already approved the work. Because approval never releases (previous question), a hold stays FUNDED after approval and can be refunded to the brand's wallet.
questions.evidence: EscrowService.refund / refundInternal, EscrowService.java:960-1013. The only guards are workspace match, assertEscrowNotBlockedByDispute (EscrowService.java:1804-1812) and requireStatus FUNDED. EscrowController.refund, EscrowController.java:152-166. The test EscrowServiceTest.refundStillSucceedsOnCancelledCollaboration (line 1191) shows refunds are intentionally permissive.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: The creator can pre-empt this only by opening a dispute first. I did not check whether the FE exposes refund on deals that have approved deliverables.

questions.question: Can a creator get money into their bank account without ops doing it by hand?
questions.why_it_matters: Creators judge the platform on getting paid. A manual payout process caps how far we can scale and adds a staffing cost.
questions.answer: Not in the production build as committed. The backend has a real RazorpayX withdrawal path, but the FE flag VITE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED defaults to false in the Dockerfile, .env.production and the publish workflow, so the Withdraw button is disabled with 'Bank transfers are being switched on'. The working path is AdminFinanceService.recordManualPayout: SUPER_ADMIN plus MFA records a bank UTR after an off-platform transfer, and the creator's wallet is debited.
questions.evidence: Dockerfile:58 (ARG VITE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED=false). .env.production:73. src/lib/api.ts:109 and :119-122 (isMoneyActionBlocked). src/pages/creator-wallet.tsx:683-697. AdminFinanceController POST /admin/finance/payouts/manual (line 91). AdminFinanceService.recordManualPayout, AdminFinanceService.java:150-272. Backend path: WalletService.requestCreatorWithdrawal, WalletService.java:250-322. WalletServiceTest has 27 tests passing in the RC surefire report.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: The repository variable vars.PAYOUTS_ENABLED on GitHub could flip this at build time. Its value is not in the repo. Whether a live RazorpayX account exists is also not visible.

questions.question: Is creator identity actually verified before we pay them out?
questions.why_it_matters: It matters for fraud, for TDS/PAN compliance and for brand trust in the 'verified creator' positioning.
questions.answer: No. The creator's identity_kyc_status only ever moves UNVERIFIED -> PENDING, self-declared through POST /onboarding/creator/kyc. No code sets it to VERIFIED. The withdrawal gate accepts PENDING.
questions.evidence: CreatorProfile.applyIdentityKyc, CreatorProfile.java:404-408, is the only writer besides the default at :217. CreatorOnboardingService.java:167. WalletService.requireIdentityKycSubmitted, WalletService.java:354-371, rejects only null/UNVERIFIED/REJECTED. A repo grep for setIdentityKycStatus/identityKycStatus= finds no VERIFIED writer.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Ops might verify PAN manually before a manual payout. That process is not in the code.

questions.question: How does the platform make money, as implemented rather than as promised?
questions.why_it_matters: It tells us whether revenue lands in the ledger automatically and what take rate customers actually see.
questions.answer: Three streams are coded. (1) Brand fee: default 10% of campaign budgetMax (7% with an ACTIVE Pro plan), debited from the brand wallet into the revenue wallet at the moment the campaign goes ACTIVE, with no refund path. (2) Creator commission: default 1500 bps (15%), deducted when escrow is released. (3) Pro subscription: Rs 4,999/month via Razorpay subscriptions; the Razorpay plan id is created lazily. AI credits and allotments are tied to the plans. All three post to the internal ledger. The combined take on a Free brand can approach ~25% of the deal value.
questions.evidence: BrandCampaignFeeService.java:40 and :173-190 (budgetMax * feeBps). V41__platform_fee_config.sql default_fee_bps 1500. application.yml:407 (PLATFORM_FEE_PERCENT default 15.00). V55__seed_billing_plans.sql (FREE 0, PRO 499900 paise, fee_bps 700, razorpay_plan_id NULL). SubscriptionService.ensureRazorpayPlanId, SubscriptionService.java:617-630. BrandCampaignFeeServiceTest (6) and Subscription* tests (68) pass in the RC surefire report.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Live fee config rows may have been edited by an admin since the seed. Real Razorpay subscription creation has not been proven at runtime.

questions.question: Can a brand get unspent money back out of the platform?
questions.why_it_matters: A prepaid wallet with no exit is a sales objection and a trust and regulatory risk (we hold no PA licence).
questions.answer: Not in-app. POST /wallet/withdraw calls creatorContext.requireCreator and rejects brands. Escrow refunds return money to the brand's platform wallet only. No Razorpay refund API is called anywhere in src/main.
questions.evidence: WalletController.java:113-125. EscrowService.refundInternal posts to the wallet via escrowBackend.refund (EscrowService.java:989-999). A grep for '/refunds|createRefund|refundPayment' under src/main/java returns 0 hits.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Ops could refund manually from the Razorpay dashboard. That is outside the code.

questions.question: Where does creator supply come from on day one?
questions.why_it_matters: Marketplace cold start. Brands who publish into an empty marketplace churn.
questions.answer: Creators who sign up themselves are discoverable by default (CreatorProfile.discoverable=true at creation). The seeded demo creators were deleted by migration. Off-platform supply is manual: an admin imports Instagram handles, and a brand's 'connect' request becomes an admin queue where the admin marks the creator contacted and sends the invite by hand.
questions.evidence: CreatorProfile.java:211. CreatorProfileSpecifications.discoverable, CreatorProfileSpecifications.java:25-28. V20260723120000__remove_seed_creators.sql (DELETE FROM creator_profiles / users). AdminExternalCreatorController POST /admin/external-creators/import (line 47). ExternalCreatorController POST /creators/external/{id}/connect (line 58). AdminCreatorConnectionController /{id}/contacted, /{id}/invite (lines 52 and 72). ExternalCreator* (30) and AdminCreatorConnection* (12) tests pass in the RC surefire report.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: The live DB creator count is unknown. I did not query production and did not claim any number.

questions.question: Do deliverables need Meta/Instagram verification before a creator is paid?
questions.why_it_matters: Meta INSTAGRAM_LOGIN has not been proven live. A hard dependency on it would stall payouts.
questions.answer: Not by default. The ON_POSTED release condition only applies after influora.escrow.release-gate.cutover-instant is set. It defaults to empty, and no deploy compose sets it, so release is ungated. Deliverable safety review is advisory only (DeliverableSafetyReviewService.getReview).
questions.evidence: application.yml:147-155 (cutover-instant: ${INFLUORA_ESCROW_RELEASE_GATE_CUTOVER_INSTANT:}). EscrowService.isPostCutover, EscrowService.java:1594-1599. A grep of deploy/*.yml finds no INFLUORA_ESCROW_RELEASE_GATE_CUTOVER_INSTANT. DeliverableSafetyReviewService.java:105-155.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: The value in the live .env on the VPS was not inspected.

questions.question: What happens if a brand goes silent after the creator delivers?
questions.why_it_matters: It sets how much creators must trust us and how heavy the ops/dispute load will be.
questions.answer: Nothing happens automatically. Release is manual and brand-triggered, and there is no timeout job. The creator's only recourse is POST /deals/{dealId}/disputes. An admin then resolves it with adminReleaseForDispute, adminRefundForDispute or adminSplitForDispute. Opening a dispute freezes both release and refund.
questions.evidence: DealController.java:186. EscrowService.adminReleaseForDispute/adminRefundForDispute/adminSplitForDispute (EscrowService.java:1247, 1286, 1333). assertEscrowNotBlockedByDispute (1804-1812). The job/ directory has no escrow auto-release job (22 jobs listed). Dispute* tests (24) pass in the RC surefire report.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Whether dispute resolution has an SLA is an ops question, not something the code shows.

questions.question: What differentiation is actually implemented, as opposed to marketed?
questions.why_it_matters: It shapes positioning claims we can defend at launch.

findings.title: A brand can refund a FUNDED escrow hold to itself after the creator delivered and the work was approved
findings.evidence: EscrowService.refundInternal (EscrowService.java:972-1013) checks only: workspace ownership, not already REFUNDED, assertEscrowNotBlockedByDispute (1804-1812), and status FUNDED. It never checks Deliverable status or whether the collaboration is past submission or approval. EscrowController.refund (EscrowController.java:152-166) requires only an OWNER/ADMIN brand member. Approval never releases money (SWP-02), so the hold is still FUNDED and refundable after approval.
findings.impact: Creators can lose payment for content already delivered and approved unless they open a dispute first. This directly contradicts the 'secured payment' value proposition and is the biggest creator-trust risk in the marketplace.
findings.recommended_fix: In refundInternal, refuse the refund (409) when any Deliverable of the hold's collaboration is SUBMITTED/APPROVED/POSTED or later, and send the brand to the dispute flow. Alternatively, only allow refunds while the collaboration is pre-submission or CANCELLED by mutual termination.
findings.reproduction: Brand funds a milestone -> creator submits -> brand approves (response released=false, NO_MILESTONE) -> brand POSTs /wallet/escrow/refund {escrowHoldId} -> hold REFUNDED and money back in the brand wallet.
findings.verification_required: A runtime reproduction in a local/staging environment, plus a unit test asserting a refund after APPROVED is rejected.

findings.title: Deliverable approval never releases payment (Deliverable.milestoneId never populated); release needs a second brand action and there is no auto-release
findings.evidence: ContractService.materializeDeliverables (ContractService.java:765-775) builds Deliverables without .milestoneId. EscrowService.tryReleaseOnApproval (EscrowService.java:729-732) returns held('NO_MILESTONE') for a null id. BrandDeliverableService.approve (BrandDeliverableService.java:191, 221-233) logs 'creator has not been paid' and returns released=false. BrandDeliverableServiceTest.java:321-323 asserts NO_MILESTONE and passes. The job/ package has no auto-release job.
findings.impact: The creator's payday depends on the brand remembering a second 'release' click. A brand that goes silent leaves money in FUNDED, where it can then be refunded (SWP-01). This creates dispute and ops load and hurts the time-to-paid retention hook.
findings.recommended_fix: Link each materialized Deliverable to its milestone (or release by collaboration's FUNDED holds on approval). Add a scheduled auto-release after N days from approval/POSTED unless disputed.
findings.reproduction: Approve any deliverable on a funded deal. The ReviewResponse paymentReleased is false and the hold remains FUNDED.
findings.verification_required: A runtime E2E on staging confirming the hold stays FUNDED after approval.

findings.title: Creator bank payout is not self-serve in the production build: withdraw is off by default and payouts are manual admin UTR entries
findings.evidence: Dockerfile:58 ARG VITE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED=false. .env.production:73 VITE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED=false. src/lib/api.ts:109 and :119-122 isMoneyActionBlocked('withdraw'). src/pages/creator-wallet.tsx:683-697 disables Withdraw and shows 'Bank transfers are being switched on'. The only production money-out path is AdminFinanceService.recordManualPayout (AdminFinanceService.java:150-272; SUPER_ADMIN plus MFA, UTR required, debits the creator wallet). Also, RazorpayXClient.isConfigured (RazorpayXClient.java:108-110) only checks the payout account is non-blank, and application.yml:404 defaults it to the non-blank placeholder 'REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_RAZORPAYX_ACCOUNT' [REDACTED-style placeholder, not a secret]. SecretsStartupValidator checks the Razorpay key/secret/webhook placeholders but not the RazorpayX account number.
findings.impact: Every creator payout needs a SUPER_ADMIN to do a manual bank transfer and enter it. The cost grows linearly with volume and payout delays hurt creator retention. If the flag is flipped without a real RazorpayX account, withdrawals fail at the gateway.
findings.recommended_fix: Decide the launch payout mode explicitly. If manual, give admins a queue of creators with withdrawable balance and a payout-request button for creators. If RazorpayX, add the payout account number to SecretsStartupValidator's placeholder checks before enabling VITE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED.
findings.reproduction: Build the FE with default args, log in as a creator, open /creator/wallet: Withdraw is disabled.
findings.verification_required: Check the GitHub repo variable PAYOUTS_ENABLED and the live bundle's flag value.

findings.title: Brand activation is blocked on a manual admin KYC approval with no notification and no in-app view of the uploaded documents
findings.evidence: CampaignValidator.validateStatusForWorkspace (CampaignValidator.java:62-68) makes ACTIVE require VERIFIED. OnboardingService.submitBrandKyc (OnboardingService.java:171-183) sets PENDING and publishes no event. AdminBrandService.verifyKyc (AdminBrandService.java:280-319) is the only way to reach VERIFIED. AdminBrandService.toDetailDto (AdminBrandService.java:763-786) returns gstin/pan strings and incorporationDoc=null. Workspace.getKycGstinDocUrl/getKycPanDocUrl (Workspace.java:288-292) and OnboardingService.resolveKycDocUrl (:205) have no production callers (grep).
findings.impact: Every new brand's first publish waits on a human with no SLA or alert. The reviewer approves without seeing the GST/PAN documents in the product, so the KYC gate adds friction without real assurance.
findings.recommended_fix: Publish a KYC-submitted event to admins (email or dashboard badge), serve presigned document URLs in BrandDetailDto via resolveKycDocUrl, and consider auto-approval on GSTIN format plus a checksum-valid PAN, with an ops audit afterwards.
findings.reproduction: Register a brand, submit KYC, try to publish: 403 WORKSPACE_NOT_VERIFIED until an admin approves. The admin brand detail shows no document links.
findings.verification_required: Confirm on staging that the admin UI shows no document; check whether an out-of-band ops alert exists.

findings.title: Brand wallet money cannot leave the platform (no brand withdrawal or refund to source)
findings.evidence: WalletController.withdraw (WalletController.java:116-125) calls creatorContext.requireCreator. EscrowService.refundInternal returns funds to the platform wallet only (EscrowService.java:989-1000). A grep for '/refunds|createRefund|refundPayment' across src/main/java finds nothing.
findings.impact: It raises a sales objection ('money is locked in'), creates support tickets that ops must handle in the Razorpay dashboard, and adds regulatory exposure as a stored-value balance (custody licence deferred).
findings.recommended_fix: Add a brand refund-to-source request (admin-approved at first) backed by the Razorpay refunds API, and state the wallet refund policy in the top-up UI.
findings.reproduction: As a brand, POST /wallet/withdraw -> rejected by requireCreator.
findings.verification_required: Confirm the FE has no brand refund request path, and confirm the ops policy.

findings.title: The 10% brand publish fee is charged on budgetMax upfront and is non-refundable even if no creator is hired or the campaign is cancelled
findings.evidence: BrandCampaignFeeService.chargeOnPublish (BrandCampaignFeeService.java:173-190, 237) computes budgetMax * feeBps at the ACTIVE transition. The service has no refund or reversal method (grep 'refund|reverse' matches only the javadoc line 40, 'deliberately no refund path'). The default brand fee is 1000 bps (Pro 700, V55__seed_billing_plans.sql). The creator commission of 1500 bps (V41__platform_fee_config.sql) applies again at release.
findings.impact: A brand pays 10% of its maximum budget before any creator accepts. Combined with the 15% creator commission, the take rate is about 25%. This invites churn after a failed first campaign and refund disputes.
findings.recommended_fix: Charge the brand fee per funded deal (on the escrow amount) instead of on budgetMax at publish, or refund the unused portion when a campaign is cancelled or completed.
findings.reproduction: Publish a campaign with budgetMax 100000 and cancel it immediately: the brand wallet stays debited 10000.
findings.verification_required: A unit/runtime test of cancel after publish showing no reversal.

findings.title: Creator identity KYC is self-declared: nothing sets VERIFIED and the payout gate accepts PENDING
findings.evidence: CreatorProfile.applyIdentityKyc (CreatorProfile.java:404-408) is the only writer, and it writes PENDING. There is no admin creator-KYC approve endpoint. WalletService.requireIdentityKycSubmitted (WalletService.java:354-371) passes PENDING. WalletServiceTest has testWithdrawalRequiresIdentityKycUnverified and testWithdrawalRequiresIdentityKycNoProfile, which pass. MeeraContextService.java:255 reports kyc_done only if VERIFIED, so it is always false.
findings.impact: Payouts can go to unverified identities (fraud and TDS/PAN exposure). Meera always tells creators their KYC is not done.
findings.recommended_fix: Add an admin creator-KYC review (approve/reject) or a PAN verification API check before the first payout. Align MeeraContextService with the chosen definition.
findings.reproduction: A creator submits KYC with any PAN format that passes DTO validation -> status PENDING -> the withdrawal gate passes.
findings.verification_required: Runtime check of the admin creator detail for any KYC action.

findings.title: The creator withdrawal calls RazorpayX before any durable Payout row exists, inside the wallet row lock (a crash after gateway success rolls back the debit)
findings.evidence: WalletService.requestCreatorWithdrawal is @Transactional (WalletService.java:249-250) and holds findByOwnerIdForUpdate. doProcessWithdrawal (381-410) posts the debit, calls razorpayXClient.initiatePayout, and only then saves the Payout. PayoutService, by contrast, persists a PENDING Payout before the gateway call so that PayoutOrphanedDebitSweepJob can reconcile it. If the process dies after RazorpayX accepts but before commit, the debit rolls back while the money has left, and no Payout row exists for the sweep to find. No test covers a gateway failure or crash after the debit (WalletServiceTest methods listed at lines 311-622).
findings.impact: A rare double-pay or unreconciled payout once VITE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED is on. It is inert while the flag is false.
findings.recommended_fix: Mirror PayoutService: persist a PENDING Payout (with the scopedKey) in its own transaction before the gateway call, and let PayoutOrphanedDebitSweepJob cover withdrawals too.
findings.reproduction: Not reproduced. It would need a fault injection between initiatePayout and commit.
findings.verification_required: Kabir/Meera fault-injection test against a stubbed RazorpayX.

findings.title: Marketplace starts empty and off-platform creator supply depends on manual admin import, contact and invite
findings.evidence: V20260723120000__remove_seed_creators.sql deletes the seed creator_profiles and users. AdminExternalCreatorController POST /admin/external-creators/import (line 47) takes a manual list of usernames. The ExternalCreatorController POST /creators/external/{id}/connect (line 58) brand request lands in AdminCreatorConnectionController, where an admin moves it through /contacted (52) and /invite (72). Self-signup creators are discoverable by default (CreatorProfile.java:211).
findings.impact: Brands who publish before supply exists see few or no creators. Every external match costs ops time, which caps how far matching can scale.
findings.recommended_fix: Before brand launch, run a creator acquisition push and bulk import. Add SLA tracking and an auto-invite email for the connection queue.
findings.reproduction: A fresh DB after migrations shows no discoverable creators until someone signs up.
findings.verification_required: A production creator count, which only ops can provide. Not queried.

area.main_uncertainty: Nothing was executed at runtime against the RC. Live env values (GitHub vars.PAYOUTS_ENABLED, VPS .env for the RazorpayX account and cutover instant) and live data (creator supply, fee config edits) were not inspected.
area.limitations: Read-only static audit plus existing test reports. No app boot, no live or production access, no payments. graphify-out/graph.json was absent in the RC, so orientation was by direct source reading. The FE was sampled, not exhaustively traced.

extra: CODE-VERIFIED FACTS (RC 115f698): (1) Brand journey: signup (self-serve, email OTP) -> KYC submit (PENDING) -> MANUAL admin approve [ops] -> Razorpay wallet top-up (self-serve, webhook plus reconciliation job) -> publish (10% of budgetMax debited, 7% on Pro) -> discover/invite, or creators apply (self-serve; external creators need MANUAL admin import/contact/invite [ops]) -> negotiate deal -> contract generate plus both sign -> fund milestone escrow from wallet -> creator submits -> brand approves (NO money moves) -> brand clicks release separately (15% commission deducted, net credited to creator wallet). (2) Creator journey: signup -> onboarding/socials -> apply or accept invite -> deliver -> wait for the brand's manual release -> withdraw DISABLED in the prod FE build -> SUPER_ADMIN manual bank transfer plus UTR entry [ops]. Identity KYC is self-declared (PENDING suffices). (3) Brand wallet money cannot be withdrawn. Escrow refunds go back to the wallet. (4) A brand can refund a funded hold at any time before a dispute, including after approval. (5) Release has no Meta/post-verification gate by default (cutover unset). Deliverable brand-safety AI is advisory. (6) Seed creators were deleted. Supply is organic signup plus manual admin import. (7) Revenue streams in code: brand publish fee, creator commission, Pro subscription Rs 4,999/month, AI credit plans. Coded retention hooks: notifications, CreatorConnectNudgeJob, Meera/Copilot AI, analytics (Meta-synced), reviews, portfolio pages, HYPE campaigns, coupon/affiliate earnings. | BUSINESS ASSUMPTIONS (not provable from code): that brands accept a non-refundable 10% fee on max budget plus the creator's 15% (~25% take); that ops can staff same-day brand KYC review and manual creator payouts at launch volume; that creators accept payment depending on the brand clicking release; that a stored brand wallet with no exit is acceptable without a PA licence; that the Meta-synced analytics differentiate us enough to retain brands. | FUTURE POSSIBILITIES (code exists but is gated or unproven): RazorpayX self-serve payouts (backend ready, FE flag off, account config unvalidated); the ON_POSTED release gate with Meta post verification (needs the cutover env plus Instagram Login approval); Meera autonomous campaign launch; affiliate settlement credits; Pro plan auto-billing. | NOT INVENTED: no customer counts, revenue, traction or market size were assumed or reported. Top go-live asks from the CEO lens: fix SWP-01 (refund after approval), fix SWP-02 (approval should release, or auto-release), decide and staff the payout mode (SWP-03), add KYC review tooling and alerting (SWP-04).
